themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints surged to 8 this past week—a 540% spike above the 1.2 weekly average—suggesting potential friction over restaurant seating, sidewalk obstruction, or noise in Greenpoint/Williamsburg's increasingly dense dining scene.
evidence: 8 outdoor dining complaints this past week vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.78)
540% increase represents sharpest proportional spike among all active complaints
Aligns with seasonal outdoor seating expansion and post-holiday restaurant activity
reporting_angles: Interview residents on McCarren Park or main commercial corridors about specific sidewalk/noise complaints tied to outdoor seating
Investigate whether NYC's outdoor dining permits (OPEN Streets program extensions) are being enforced or if unlicensed seating is proliferating

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Accumulation
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints jumped to 10 this past week—a 321% spike from the 2.4 weekly baseline—indicating a potential debris or street-clutter crisis, possibly tied to e-bike or dockless scooter abandonment.
evidence: 10 abandoned bike complaints this past week vs. 2.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.08)
321% increase suggests rapid or visible accumulation in specific blocks or parks
Potential link to e-bike/scooter sharing services or post-holiday dumping
reporting_angles: Map clusters of abandoned bike reports in the district; visit hotspot blocks to photograph and assess scale
Interview NYPD or Sanitation about removal protocols; contact bike-share operators (Citi Bike, e-bike companies) about compliance

themes_detail.label: Missing Street Signs Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints exploded to 8 last week—a 482% increase from the 1.4 weekly average—creating potential wayfinding and safety hazards across the district amid ongoing DOT budget constraints.
evidence: 8 missing street sign complaints last week vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.73)
482% increase suggests either recent vandalism, weather damage, or systemic maintenance backlog
Safety concern if affecting intersections, pedestrian crossings, or transit areas
reporting_angles: File FOIL request to DOT for street sign removal/replacement work orders in CD 301 over past 30 days
Walk high-traffic intersections (Kent Ave, McCarren Park area, Graham Ave) to verify missing signage and photograph patterns

themes_detail.label: Tree Planting Request Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Tree planting requests skyrocketed to 3 two weeks ago—a 2300% spike from the 0.1 weekly average—signaling possible grassroots environmental activism or a response to a visible tree-loss incident in the neighborhood.
evidence: 3 tree planting requests 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69)
2300% proportional spike is largest anomaly in dataset; highest z-score suggests genuine outlier event
May indicate community organizer campaign, response to street tree removals, or climate-focused initiative
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks to determine if a tree removal or planting halt triggered these requests; review any recent CB or community group meetings on green infrastructure
Identify the three complainants via 311 database and interview about what prompted their requests (coordinated campaign vs. spontaneous)

themes_detail.label: Building Facade Deterioration Trend
themes_detail.summary: Paint/plaster complaints reached 34 three weeks ago—a 118% spike from the 15.6 weekly average—coinciding with 1,293 recent DOB permit filings, suggesting facade work backlog or accelerated building aging across the district.
evidence: 34 paint/plaster complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 15.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.66)
118% spike aligns with 1,293 recent DOB filings (746 alterations, 202 new buildings, 39 demolitions)
Possible systemic issue: ongoing gentrification/renovation driving complaints, or deferred maintenance on older buildings
reporting_angles: Cross-reference paint/plaster complaint addresses with DOB permit data to see if complaints cluster on permitted vs. unpermitted buildings
Interview residents on blocks with high facade complaints; investigate whether landlords are complying with Local Law 11 (facade inspection) requirements
